transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thanks. Um… I guess what brings me in is I’ve been feeling a little foggy in my head lately. Nothing huge, I don’t think, but I’m making small mistakes in my client notes and sometimes I’ll forget what I was just about to do. That’s not really like me, so I figured I should get it checked out, if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I mean, a little, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but lately I’ll wake up and there’s this heavy, kind of empty feeling in my chest. I can still get through my shift and talk to people okay, so it’s not like I’m falling apart, but inside I feel pretty sad and flat. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been feeling fatigued or like you don’t have much energy lately, even if you’re not doing anything physically taxing?

Yeah… a bit. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m completely wiped out or anything, but even on days where I haven’t really done much, my body feels kind of worn down. Like helping a client shower, or even carrying groceries in, feels like it takes more out of me than it should. I don’t know if that counts as fatigue exactly, but it’s been noticeable.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you normally like doing?

I’m not totally sure… I still do things, you know, like if there’s something I need to do I’ll do it. I wouldn’t say I’ve completely lost interest. Maybe things just feel a little less fun or I’m not as motivated to start them, but I don’t know if that’s serious enough to count. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating, making decisions, or thinking clearly lately?

Yeah… a little. I don’t want to overstate it, but honestly that’s kind of part of why I came in. My head just feels foggy sometimes, and I’ll catch myself making small mistakes in my client notes, or I’ll walk into a room and forget what I was about to do. It’s not like I can’t function, but it’s not really like me either… if that makes sense.
Have you noticed that you take less pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy, even things you looked forward to before?

I guess… not really in a big way? I mean, I still can enjoy things once I’m doing them. Maybe I’m just slower to get started or I don’t get as excited beforehand like I used to, but I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you found that you don’t feel pleasure or enjoyment from things you used to like, even when you’re actually doing them?

I don’t think so… not exactly. Like, if I’m actually doing something I usually like, I can still enjoy it some. It maybe doesn’t feel as exciting as it used to, but I wouldn’t say there’s no pleasure there. I’m not sure if I’m explaining that right.
Would you say that you’ve lost interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even when you’re actually doing them?

I’d say… not really, no. I mean, I’m not jumping at things the way I used to, maybe, but once I’m actually doing them I can still get some enjoyment out of it. So I don’t think I’ve lost interest or pleasure, at least not in the way you’re asking. Does that answer it okay?
Would you say that the enjoyment you get from those activities feels noticeably less compared to before, even when you're actually doing them?

Maybe a little less, but not in a way that feels, like, dramatic or anything. I still get something out of it when I’m there doing it. It’s more like… maybe I’m not as enthusiastic as I remember being before. But I wouldn’t want to say I’m not enjoying things. Is that distinction helpful?

Have you noticed that you don’t feel like doing things that you used to look forward to, even things that used to make you happy, and that you really don’t get the same satisfaction out of them anymore?

I guess I wouldn’t put it that strongly. I haven’t really noticed that I don’t want to do things at all, or that they don’t satisfy me anymore. Maybe I’m a little slower to get going, but if I do something I used to like, it’s still… it’s still okay, still kind of good. So I don’t think that’s really been happening. Is that what you mean?
Would you say that you’ve lost interest in almost all activities, even ones you used to really enjoy, most of the time?

No, I don’t think I’d say almost all activities, or most of the time. That sounds stronger than what I’m experiencing. I mean, I can be a little less motivated sometimes, but I still do enjoy things when I do them. So… I don’t think I’ve lost interest like that, if that makes sense.
Would you say that most days, you feel sad or down for most of the day, even if you’re able to function and get things done?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still getting to work and doing what I need to do, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything. But most mornings lately I wake up with this kind of heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I can talk to people and get through my shift, but inside I feel pretty sad and flat a lot of the day. Does that answer it okay?
Would you say that most days, you feel sad or down for most of the day, even if you’re able to function and get things done?

Yeah… I think I would say that, though I don’t want to make it sound too dramatic. Lately I’ve been waking up with this heavy, kind of empty feeling in my chest. I can still get through my shift and talk to people and all that, but inside I feel pretty sad and flat for a lot of the day. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Have you found yourself feeling like you’re not good enough, or that you’ve been blaming yourself for things more than usual?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I try not to sit there and beat myself up, but I do catch myself replaying stuff with my tío before he passed. Like, I keep thinking I should’ve called more, or gone to see him sooner, and then I feel like I failed him somehow, like as family. I know maybe that’s not totally fair, but it’s hard not to go there.
Would you say that you’ve been feeling like you’re not good enough or worthless nearly every day, even if it’s just in the background?

Yeah… I mean, “worthless” feels like a strong word, and I don’t want to overstate it. But nearly every day it’s kind of there in the background, especially about my tío. I keep replaying what I should’ve done before he died—called more, visited sooner—and then I end up feeling like I failed him as family. I know maybe that’s not totally fair, but it still hits me that way.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have been slower than usual, or that you feel restless or fidgety more often than before?

Maybe more on the restless side, yeah. I don’t think my speech has been slower or anything—at least I hope not—but there was a stretch where I just couldn’t really sit still. Like if I stopped moving, the grief was going to catch up with me, so I kept making little errands for myself, calling people, doing chores… just staying busy. I don’t know if that’s what you mean, but it was definitely more than usual.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, even when you’re actually doing them, like you don’t get any pleasure out of them anymore?

I don’t think I’d say completely lost interest, no. Like… some things don’t feel as easy to enjoy right now, but if I’m actually doing them, I can still get something out of it sometimes. So I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
